brand_notes.materials: Dimension-Polyant X-Pac VX21/VX42 or Challenge ECOPAK EPX200/EPX240 face fabric, 500D/1000D Cordura abrasion panels wherever the bag touches a tube, MIL-spec webbing and MIL-spec BLACK binding tape on every edge. The black binding outline around a bright or printed panel is the single strongest brand cue - a flat single-colour bag with unbound edges will not read as Oveja Negra.
brand_notes.prints: Several colourways are PRINTS, not flat colours, and must be rendered as patterns: Serape (a woven Mexican blanket print - dense horizontal multi-colour stripes running across the panel, colours vary bag to bag), Multicam Black (dark grey/olive/black camo), Party Animal (bright confetti/splatter), Denim (heather blue weave), Wack Pack (random mismatched scrap panels, every bag different - see the Gearslammer photos where one bag is black + olive camo + blue + orange + yellow with purple and teal webbing). Highlighter is a flat fluoro yellow-green, Raspberry Beret a flat magenta.
brand_notes.logo: Hand-scrawled 'OVEJA NEGRA(TM)' wordmark. On the frame bags and the Bolt-On it is a large screen print on the lower flank (reflective on the 1/2 Pack and the Bolt-On). On the small bags it is instead a small white woven label sewn into a seam.
brand_notes.frame_bag_strap_system: ON's signature: the top edge of every frame bag carries a CONTINUOUS SLOTTED WEBBING LADDER, and the top tube straps are separate removable Velcro One-Wrap tabs threaded through it wherever you like ('fully adjustable/removable top tube strap design allows for the addition of top tube bags without conflicting strap placement'). This is why studio photos of the same bag show 3 or 4 tabs in different positions - the count is not fixed. Render the ladder, then place tabs on it.
brand_notes.photo_orientation: Every Oveja Negra studio elevation and every size chart is drawn with the FRONT OF THE BIKE AT THE RIGHT, except the Bolt-On Snack Pack chart and photos, which are drawn front-at-left.

products.name: Snack Pack

From it the top edge sweeps forward and down in a convex curve to a low, tightly rounded far end, and the bottom edge is flat. Width is a constant 2in top to bottom: plastic side inserts hold the flanks flat and parallel, so this is a wedge in ELEVATION only, not in plan. Black binding around the whole perimeter.

products.name: Chuckbucket Handlebar Snack Bag

products.dims_note: CORRECTION. hgt was 20.1, which was a 30% blend of the 7-10in range and is not what the rule asks for. The dimension rule says take the MINIMUM of a height range, so hgt = the 7in structured body with the collar collapsed = 17.8cm. Diameter is a single published figure, 4.5in = 11.4cm. Cross-check: pi/4 x 11.4^2 x 17.8 = 1.82L against ON's '1L+' rating - comfortable, and the extra 3in of collar takes it well past that.

render.basis: PUBLISHED RANGE, minimum taken. ON's chart 'MODEL: chuckbucket' dimensions the bag as a 7in structured body with a 3in soft collar drawn above it, i.e. a 7-10in height range. Drawn at the 7in body with the hex-ripstop collar collapsed onto the rim. NOTE: I am adding a render block here against the team-lead's instruction to omit it for the Chuckbucket as a 'zipped and fixed' bag - it is not zipped and its height is not fixed. It closes with a drawcord on a soft extension collar, which is exactly the variable-height case the block exists for. Flagging rather than silently following the list.

Above the structured rim sits a SOFT BLACK 70d HEX-RIPSTOP EXTENSION COLLAR about 3in tall that gathers on a drawcord - in every studio photo the collar is slouched open above the rigid body, which is exactly how it should render. The body carries the colourway fabric; the collar, the mesh, the binding and the base are always BLACK regardless of colourway.

products.name: Front End Loader Dry Bag Mount
products.dims_raw: Max. Width: 11 inches; Accepts 8-20 liter dry bags
products.dims_note: Only ONE figure is published: 'Max. Width: 11 inches' = 27.9cm, and that is the len here. THE PRODUCT ITSELF IS NOT A CYLINDER - photos 1 and 2 show a flat, semi-rigid, roughly SQUARE Cordura panel with rounded corners, about as tall as it is wide, so the bare product is close to 27.9 x 27.9 x 2cm. The 18cm wid/hgt carried here stand in for a ~15L user-supplied dry bag so the barroll slot has something to render, and are NOT maker figures. Left as stored; do not treat 18 as verified.

render.basis: NO published height of any kind, and no unfurled figure to correct - the Loader is a flat panel and the height belongs to the rider's dry bag. Included anyway because this is the product in my set most likely to be drawn wrong: the ON part is a plate, but the barroll slot must draw a cylinder. 18cm is the drawn diameter of a mid-range (~15L) dry bag. On-bike photo front-end-loader-...-4.jpg shows a fat-bike setup with a dry bag reading noticeably larger than 18cm against the 32mm bar, so 18 is a conservative middle of the 8-20L range rather than a measurement - scale it with the dry bag size the configurator picks.

geometry.notes: The Oveja Negra part is a stiffened black Cordura plate, roughly square with generously rounded corners, bound all round, with a horizontal seam across it at about 55% height and a vertical webbing spine up the middle of the front face. It carries no volume of its own. What the barroll slot should actually draw is the ASSEMBLY: this plate standing vertically between the bar and the load, plus the rider's own 8-20L dry bag lying horizontally across the bars in front of it, held off the bar and slightly low by the plate. Photo ...-4.jpg shows exactly this with a white dry bag.

products.closure_note: The Loader has no closure of its own - the closure belongs to the user's dry bag, normally a rolltop clipped at both ends.

products.name: Superwedgie 2.0 Frame Bag
products.dims_raw: ON size chart 'MAKE: Frame / MODEL: Super Wedgie', Small silhouette: 13" (top edge), 9" (tall rear edge), 14" (long lower diagonal), 1.5" (short edge at the pointed end). No width is labelled anywhere on the chart.
products.dims_note: REAL ERROR FOUND IN THE STORED WIDTH. I downloaded and read ON's Superwedgie chart directly. The 1.5" callout is a VERTICAL arrow measuring the short edge at the pointed (head tube) end of the panel - it is in exactly the position where the Bodega charts put their '2"/2.5" head tube edge'. It is NOT the bag's width, and a previous pass read it as one. A 3.8cm-wide bag is impossible against ON's published 3L: the panel area is about 377 sq cm, which at 3.8cm gives 1.4L. I have therefore set wid to 6.0cm, matching the 1/2 Pack (also 3L) and close to the Bodega S at 6.3cm. THIS IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A MAKER FIGURE - ON publishes no width for the Superwedgie. len (13") and hgt (9") are chart-verified and unchanged.

geometry.notes: THIS IS THE SHAPE THAT GETS MIS-MODELLED. It is a four-sided panel, not a right triangle. (1) A straight horizontal TOP TUBE EDGE, 13in. (2) At the FRONT, a very short near-vertical HEAD TUBE EDGE of only 1.5in - so the front is a sharp but blunt-tipped wedge nose, roughly a 39deg included angle, not a needle point. (3) A long straight DOWN TUBE EDGE of 14in running from that nose down and REARWARD, lying on the down tube. (4) At the REAR, a free near-vertical edge 9in tall, leaning slightly forward at its base, facing the seat tube but not touching it. The bag therefore fills the FRONT of the front triangle - it starts where the top tube and down tube nearly meet at the head tube and deepens rearward as the tubes diverge, then simply stops, leaving the seat tube / bottom bracket corner open. It is deep at the back and shallow at the front, which is the opposite of what people usually build. Black binding on every edge; a black Cordura reinforcement panel wraps the whole nose.

products.name: 1/2 Pack 2.0 Frame Bag
products.dims_raw: ON size chart 'Make: Frame / Model: Half Pack 2.0', S/M sheet: Small = 16.5" long x 4.5" tall, annotated '*multi-positionable top straps'. No width labelled.
products.dims_note: REAL CORRECTION, and the previous note was wrong that ON publishes no dimensions for the 1/2 Pack 2.0. The charts DO exist - they are served as two plain image files (1_480x480.png = L/XL, 2_480x480.png = S/M) rather than under a 'sizechart' filename, which is presumably why an earlier pass missed them. I downloaded and read both. Small: len 38 -> 41.9 (16.5"), hgt 12 -> 11.4 (4.5"). Width is still not published; wid left at the stored 6.0 and it is NOT maker-verified. A small triangular tab hangs down from the bottom edge just behind that bevel. products.name: Gearjammer Seat Bag
products.dims_raw: ON size chart 'MAKE: Seat / MODEL: Gearjammer', Large (6-12 liters): 22.5" @ max (no compression), 12.5" @ min (full compression), 7.5" dia.; *seat rail-tire clearance = 8" min
products.dims_note: MATERIAL CORRECTION UNDER THE NEW RULE. I downloaded and read ON's chart directly. len must be the UNFURLED figure, 22.5" = 57.2cm; the stored 39.4 was a 30% blend of the 12.5-22.5in compression range, which the rule no longer allows. The 7.5in is a single published diameter, not a range, so wid and hgt are both 19.1 and there is no min-height reduction to apply. Volume check: 57.2 x 19.1 x 19.1 = 20.9L box against the 12L max rating, ratio 1.7 - inside the 1.0-2.5 band for a soft tapered bag. This bag is 45% longer than the model previously had it.

geometry.notes: A long blade, and unusually for a seat pack it is DEEPEST IN THE MIDDLE AND AT THE TAIL, narrowing toward the nose where it has to squeeze past the seatpost. The bottom edge is dead straight - that is the HDPE frame sheet - and the flanks are flat stiffened panels, so the section is a rounded rectangle rather than a tube. The tail end is a squared roll; at full compression the whole rear half collapses and the tail becomes a rounded blade at 12.5in overall. Large black Cordura panels cover the nose and form a V across the flank, with the colourway fabric showing through the middle and the rolled tail.

PHOTO CROSS-CHECK on the on-bike shot gearslammer-...-3.jpg, scaling from the Ergon saddle (taken as 270mm long): the bag measures ~275mm long, which supports len 28; but its maximum depth measures ~166mm, which suggests hgt is nearer 16cm than the stored 12. A 28 x 12 x 12 box is exactly 4.0L against a 2-4L rating (ratio 1.0), which is tight for a soft tapered roll-top; 28 x 12 x 16 gives 5.4L, ratio 1.35, which is more typical. I have NOT changed the number because the photo is a three-quarter view and foreshortened - treat hgt as the least reliable figure in this record.

products.name: Bootlegger Fork Bag (Direct Mount)
products.dims_raw: ON size chart 'MAKE: Fork / MODEL: Bootlegger': 4.5" dia., 10" closed, 14" open. CAPACITY 2 liters; fits a 32 oz Nalgene or a 40 oz wide Klean Kanteen.
products.dims_note: REAL CORRECTION, and the previous note was wrong that ON gives no dimensions - the size chart exists and I downloaded and read it. It gives 4.5in dia (11.4cm, was 11) and a 10"-14" height range. Per the rule hgt is the MINIMUM of that range, the rolled-down 10" = 25.4cm (was 28, which was unsourced and sat between the two). Volume check: pi/4 x 11.4^2 x 25.4 = 2.59L against the stated 2L, ratio 1.3.

geometry.notes: Upright padded cylinder, very slightly flared - the chart's dashed unrolled outline is wider at the mouth than at the base - and flattened on the fork side where the alloy frame bolts through. The defining surface detail is THREE CHEVRON SEAM LINES stepping down the body: each runs horizontally from one edge, kinks down at a shallow diagonal across the middle and continues horizontally to the other edge. They appear in all four studio photos and are drawn on ON's own chart, so they are structural, not decorative. Black binding round the base; the roll and its buckle strap sit proud above the body.

closure.hardware: single side-release buckle on a urethane-coated webbing strap across the rolled mouth

straps.notes: the bag's only strap - ON's whole pitch is 'CAGE-LESS / STRAP-LESS'

details.frame: proprietary aluminium alloy frame, made in the USA, hidden behind the bag's flat face; the bag bolts straight through it to the fork
details.padding: padded body, quilted between the chevron seams

mount.notes: NO CAGE AND NO STRAPS. It bolts directly to a standard three-pack fork mount through its own alloy frame, so it sits closer to the fork leg and lower than a strapped bottle-in-a-cage setup, and the outboard face is completely clean. Mouth up, roll and buckle at the top.
